concept.name: Swap dealer category
concept.definition: A trader category in the CFTC's Disaggregated Commitments of Traders report: an entity that deals primarily in swaps for a commodity and uses the futures markets to manage or hedge the risk associated with those swaps transactions, whether its counterparties are speculators such as hedge funds or traditional commercial clients.
concept.intuition: These are banks and dealers whose futures positions are the warehouse for risk they took on from OTC swap clients — the futures leg is the hedge, not the bet.
concept.mechanics: The category was created in 2009 on the recommendation of the CFTC's 2008 Staff Report on Commodity Swap Dealers & Index Traders, splitting swap dealers out of the legacy commercial category. Swap dealer open interest is reported long, short, and spreading; commodity index business typically appears here because dealers hedge index swaps with futures.
concept.failure_modes: Some swap-dealer-classified traders also conduct physical-commodity commercial activity, blurring the line with the PMPU category; classification reflects predominant activity and can change. The category is related to, but not identical with, the commodity index trader category in the CIT supplement — direct index investors using futures fall under managed money or other reportables instead.
concept.misconceptions: A large swap-dealer long is not a speculative bet — it typically hedges short exposure from client index swaps. The category also does not map to the legal registration definition of 'swap dealer' under Dodd-Frank (which carries a de minimis notional threshold); it is a COT reporting classification.
concept.example: An investment bank that sells a commodity index swap to a pension fund buys the underlying basket of futures to hedge; its futures longs are reported in the Disaggregated COT under swap dealers.
